message.content:
The “best” movie of 2020 is a matter of taste and criteria, but if you look at critical consensus, audience reception, and award recognition, **“Nomadland”** often comes out on top.

| Why “Nomadland” is a strong contender | Details |
|--------------------------------------|---------|
| **Critical acclaim** | 94 % on Rotten Tomatoes (critics) and 8.5/10 on Metacritic. |
| **Audience reception** | 86 % on Rotten Tomatoes (audience) and 8.2/10 on IMDb. |
| **Awards** | Won the Academy Award for Best Picture, Best Director (Chloé Zhao), and Best Actress (Frances McDormand). It also swept the Golden Globes for Best Motion Picture – Drama and Best Director. |
| **Cultural impact** | The film sparked conversations about the gig economy, rural America, and the definition of “home.” |

Other films that were highly regarded in 2020 include:

| Film | Highlights |
|------|------------|
| **“Parasite”** | Though released in 2019, it dominated 2020 awards season with 4 Oscars, including Best Picture. |
| **“Soul”** | Pixar’s animated feature received universal praise for its music, storytelling, and philosophical depth. |
| **“The Trial of the Chicago 7”** | A powerful political drama that earned an Oscar nomination for Best Picture and a Best Original Screenplay win. |
| **“The Father”** | Anthony Hopkins’ performance earned him an Oscar for Best Actor. |

If you’re looking for a film that blends critical success, audience love, and award recognition, **“Nomadland”** is the most celebrated movie of 2020.
